proof_summary: For the odd-indexed terms, the error \(b_{2m+1}e-a_{2m+1}\) is identified, via matching initial values and a recurrence obtained by twice integrating by parts, with \((-1)^{m+1}(m+1)!^{-1}\int_0^1 e^x(x(1-x))^{m+1}\,dx\); bounding the integral by \(e\) makes this error (even after multiplication by a linear factor) tend to zero. A bridge identity expresses each even-indexed error as a linear combination of two odd-indexed errors, so both parity subsequences of the ratios converge to \(e\), and hence so does the full sequence.
